content.text:
VERDICT: LGTM

The change is structurally clean and improves the codebase's coherence.

- **Right unit of logic.** The common RFC 7807 construction stays centralized in `ProblemDetails`. The new four-arg `build(ex, status, detail, fields)` delegates to the existing three-arg overload and only layers on the `errors` member — proper reuse, no duplication of the title/timestamp/schemaValidationErrors boilerplate.

- **Converges on the established pattern.** The six field-error handlers now match the exact shape of the pre-existing `ProblemDetail` handlers (`DuplicateIdentityExceptionHandler`, `DailyOwnerLimitExceptionHandler`): `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail>>`, `ProblemDetails.build(...)`, `response.send(ResponseEntity.status(...).body(detail))`. The previously divergent `OwnerFieldErrors` contract is retired, so a maintainer now sees one consistent error-body idiom across all handlers.

- **Dead code removed cleanly.** `OwnerFieldErrors` is deleted and has no remaining references in `src/main/java`.

- **No catch-all growth.** Each handler keeps only its distinct detail message and field name; the shared concern lives in the helper. The overload is a natural, additive extension rather than a grab-bag.

The per-handler repetition of `ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST).body(detail)` is inherent to the one-class-per-exception OfficeFloor convention and matches the rest of the package, so it's idiomatic rather than a smell.
